headline: Effort to bypass the Electoral College could hit key milestone
pages: A national effort to ensure the presidential popular vote winner takes office may soon reach a major milestone after Democratic gains in this month's midterms. The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact would have states award their electoral votes to the national popular vote winner. It now holds 222 electoral votes. Next year Democrats will fully control Arizona, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Nevada and Wisconsin, which together carry 61 electoral votes, and any four of them would push the compact past the 270 needed. Governors and incoming governors in Pennsylvania and Nevada have said they are open to signing, while others have not weighed in.

No Republican-led state has joined, and the party is largely not unified on the issue. Political, practical and legal hurdles remain, including whether battleground states will give up their influence. Backers say they are more confident than ever about the 2028 race. Source: NPR.
